the best report shows that brother Leo who's about 15 he's watching and he sees that this is how he describes it that this thing dealt harshly with Francis afterwards Francis was injured

as_told.title: St. Francis's flaming torch on Mount La Verna

plain: Saint Francis of Assisi, the medieval Christian saint, is said to have received the stigmata, wounds like those of Christ, on a mountain in Italy, and a religion scholar named Diana Pasulka retells it from the old sources: his young companion Brother Leo, about 15, watched a being described as a seraph, a kind of fiery angel, deal harshly with Francis and leave him injured. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, crediting Pasulka and her book American Cosmic, describes it as a spinning disk, atmospheric sparks and telepathic talk, says the original wording is closer to a flaming torch than Christ or an angel, and suggests the wounds were electromagnetic burns. If so, one of the most famous saints' visions would have been an encounter with a craft.
